claims.text: The as-cast AlCoCrFeNi2.1 eutectic alloy has a fine lamellar FCC/B2 dual-phase microstructure with an interlamellar spacing of about 2 μm.
The as-cast AlCoCrFeNi2.1 alloy has low room-temperature tensile ductility and undergoes catastrophic interfacial cracking.
Stress concentration at FCC/B2 phase boundaries causes the stated low ductility and catastrophic cracking.
Severe plastic deformation at 400–600 °C will fragment the lamellae and roughen their interfaces.
Annealing at 700–800 °C under 2–5 GPa hydrostatic pressure will coalesce the fragmented interfaces into a patterned reticulated network rather than a continuous lamellar stack.
The 400–800 °C treatment range is below the eutectic melting point and above the recrystallization threshold for the B2/BCC phases in this alloy.
The resulting topology will consist of a discontinuous patterned network of B2 precipitates in an FCC matrix, or the inverse phase arrangement.
A reticulated Laves-phase structure can improve ductility in a refractory high-entropy alloy.
Extreme hydrostatic pressure suppresses void nucleation and crack propagation at FCC/B2 interfaces in AlCoCrFeNi2.1.
Extreme pressure promotes interface migration and Ostwald-ripening-like coalescence driven by strain energy stored during SPD.
Coherent interfaces can facilitate dislocation transmission and relieve stress concentrations that otherwise cause premature crack initiation.
The proposed patterned FCC/B2 interfaces will be coherent or semicoherent and permit enhanced dislocation transmission.
The proposed treatment will raise room-temperature tensile elongation above 10% while increasing fracture strength without a proportional reduction in yield strength.
The treatment will replace interfacial cracking and catastrophic failure with uniform plastic deformation.
A pressure of 2–5 GPa is sufficient to cause interface coalescence without amorphization, phase decomposition, or excessive grain coarsening.
The mechanism will fail above the B2-phase stability limit or when pressure is too low to prevent void nucleation.
Conventional HIP at approximately 1200 °C and 200 MPa for 1 hour is an established processing condition for a refractory high-entropy alloy.
Comparing HITMT at 500 °C plus 3 GPa/750 °C against HIP at 1200 °C/200 MPa isolates extreme pressure as the critical causal variable.

contradictions.description: These fields characterize the as-cast AlCoCrFeNi2.1 alloy as low-ductility and catastrophically cracking, whereas the cited same-system evidence reports 25.6% engineering elongation, 944 MPa fracture stress, and a balanced high-strength/high-ductility response. This is a grounding conflict rather than a contradiction between two hypothesis fields.

The experiment claims to isolate extreme pressure, but Groups A and B differ simultaneously in pressure, temperature, deformation history, and annealing schedule. Similar or different outcomes therefore cannot uniquely attribute causality to extreme pressure.
